# The hybrid taxonomy

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_data.py. Edit the workbook, not this file. -->

Both scopes of the Knowledge Mapping Page — Internal GCDC and the GCC
Network — are coded against one three-level structure:

**7 CF domains** → **23 CF competencies** → **65 Level-3 expertise areas**

Levels 1 and 2 are the Gulf CDC Public Health Competency Framework, in its
own wording and numbering. Level 3 is this project's own layer: the
expertise areas staff and network members actually named in the survey,
each placed under exactly one competency.

## 1. Framework fit

Not every expertise area people named falls inside the Competency
Framework's scope. Rather than force them, each area carries a fit flag:

| Framework Fit | Areas | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Direct | 45 | the area sits squarely inside the competency as the framework defines it |
| Nearest fit — outside CF scope | 18 | research, laboratory/clinical and workforce-education expertise the framework does not cover; placed under the closest competency and marked |
| Added in v6 — CF coverage | 2 | added so a competency the framework requires is not left without a Level-3 area |

## 2. Counting rules

People are coded at **Level 3 only**. Competency and domain figures roll
up from there, and someone who holds two areas under one competency counts
**once** for that competency — so competency holders are distinct people,
not expertise tags.

An area counts only where it is held as **core** expertise — what someone
would be called on to do or teach — not mere awareness of the subject:

| Holders | Status |
|---|---|
| 0 | 🔴 No core expert |
| 1 | 🟠 Single core expert (single point of failure) |
| 2 | 🟡 Thin coverage |
| 3 or more | 🟢 Adequate |

Two competencies are **behavioural**:

- **7.3 Build Relationships and Communicate with Influence**
- **7.5 Apply Self-Awareness and Reflective Practice**

They describe how someone works rather than a body of knowledge, so they
have no Level-3 area by design. They are reported as *Not mapped —
behavioural* in neutral grey and are **never counted as a gap**. That is
why 21, not 23, competencies can carry holders.

## 3. Profile Level

Profile Level is the CF proficiency band. It is derived from the years of
experience each person reported in the survey, using the workbook's own
`Profile_Level_Rules` sheet — the portal never hard-codes the thresholds:

| Years of experience | CF proficiency | Career stage | Depth score |
|---|---|---|---|
| Less than 2 years | Competent | Entry | 2 |
| 2–5 years | Competent | Entry | 3 |
| 6–10 years | Proficient | Mid-career | 4 |
| More than 10 years | Expert | Senior | 5 |

Where Profile Level is sorted or filtered, the order is
**Expert > Proficient > Competent**.

- Why these bands: the toolkit defines three proficiency levels — Competent, Proficient, Expert — "based on training, experience and performance", and tags training to staff levels entry / mid / senior (Ch. 7). It sets no year thresholds, so the survey bands are mapped to those three stages: up to 5 years = entry (Competent), 6–10 = mid-career (Proficient), more than 10 = senior (Expert).
- Depth keeps a step between <2 and 2–5 years so the earlier rule (juniors under 2 years rank lowest) still holds inside Competent.
- This replaces the earlier 5-level composite (Aware → Strategic). Seniority and external consultation now count only in Impact, not in the level.
- Source: the internal staff survey question on years of professional experience. Haya Sulaiman Alothaimeen and Abdullah Alqahtani are not in the survey — their years are carried from the Phase-2 workbook.

## 4. From the old taxonomy to the CF domains

The portal previously used 10 knowledge-management domains and 30
sub-domains of this project's own making. Every Level-3 area kept its
identity and moved under a CF competency; this table shows where each old
domain's areas ended up. An old domain can map to more than one CF domain,
which is the point of the move — the framework splits distinctions the old
structure ran together.

Two labels in the first column are not previous domains: *Portal taxonomy
review* marks the six areas created during the portal's own taxonomy
review, and *New in v6* the two added for CF coverage. Both are now part
of the workbook taxonomy like any other area.

| Origin | CF domain(s) | Areas |
|---|---|---|
| Data, Digital Health & Health Informatics | D3 (8) | 8 |
| Health Policy, Systems & Strategy | D4 (2)<br>D5 (2)<br>D6 (2)<br>D7 (1) | 7 |
| Health Promotion, Education & Workforce | D2 (2)<br>D4 (5) | 7 |
| Research & Scientific Practice | D2 (1)<br>D3 (4)<br>D6 (2) | 7 |
| Epidemiology & Surveillance | D1 (1)<br>D2 (1)<br>D3 (4) | 6 |
| Portal taxonomy review (Claude Code) | D1 (3)<br>D2 (2)<br>D3 (1) | 6 |
| Quality, Governance & Project Management | D4 (4)<br>D5 (1)<br>D7 (1) | 6 |
| Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases | D1 (3)<br>D2 (2) | 5 |
| Public Health Emergency & Health Security | D1 (5) | 5 |
| Clinical & Specialized Practice | D1 (3)<br>D2 (1) | 4 |
| Cross-Cutting Professional Skills | D6 (1)<br>D7 (1) | 2 |
| New in v6 | D2 (1)<br>D5 (1) | 2 |

separately and never merged in. Areas with no core holder are the gaps,
listed in full on the page's Gaps tab.
